title: Multilevel Inheritance
summary: Understand transitive inheritance chains (Grandparent -> Parent -> Child) and bottom-up method dispatch.
learningObjectives: Define Multilevel Inheritance and understand the Grandparent -> Parent -> Child chain
Explain transitivity: how a subclass inherits members from all ancestors in its lineage
Trace linear method lookup across three or more inheritance tiers
Analyze object memory layout for deeply chained inheritance structures
Model real-world taxonomic classifications cleanly using multilevel hierarchies
expectedOutcomes: Ability to build multi-tier class hierarchies in Java without code duplication
Clear understanding of how transitivity flows state and behavior down to leaf subclasses

activities.title: The Family Generations Analogy
activities.content:
Think about three generations in a family:

```text
Grandparent (Generation 1)
    ↓
Parent (Generation 2)
    ↓
Child (Generation 3)
```

Your Grandparent established a family estate and has blue eyes. Your Parent inherited the family estate and blue eyes from the Grandparent, and became a master chef. When you are born as the Child, what do you inherit?

You inherit the family estate and blue eyes (from your Grandparent), the cooking skills (from your Parent), AND you can learn computer programming yourself!

In Java, **Multilevel Inheritance** creates this exact generational chain. The lowest class inherits all visible fields and methods from every ancestor class all the way up to `java.lang.Object`!

activities.title: Multilevel Inheritance: Inheritance in a Chain
Multilevel Hierarchy: Device -> Computer -> Laptop
activities.description: Trace how fields and methods flow down from Device to Computer to Laptop.

steps.description: Device is the Grandparent superclass providing brand and powerOn().
Computer extends Device, adding ramGB and runDiagnostics().
Laptop extends Computer, adding weightKg and showPortability().
myLaptop has access to powerOn() (from Grandparent), runDiagnostics() (from Parent), and showPortability() (from Child).

activities.title: Biological Classification: Animal -> Mammal -> Dog
activities.description: Observe transitivity in action with a classic biological taxonomy hierarchy.

steps.description: Mammal extends Animal and introduces warmBlooded and feedMilk().
Dog extends Mammal and adds breed and bark().
The Dog instance exhibits full transitivity, accessing fields and methods from all 3 levels.

activities.codeSnippet:
Dog retriever = new Dog("Golden Retriever");
retriever.breathe();  // Animal
retriever.feedMilk(); // Mammal
retriever.bark();     // Dog

questions.question: What is Multilevel Inheritance in Java?
options: A class inheriting from multiple classes at the exact same time
A chain of inheritance where a subclass extends another subclass (Grandparent -> Parent -> Child)
A class having multiple constructors
Inheriting methods without inheriting any fields
questions.explanation: Multilevel inheritance represents a sequential chain of inheritance where class C extends B, and B extends A.

questions.question: If Class C extends Class B, and Class B extends Class A, what is the relationship between C and A?
options: C and A are completely unrelated
A is an indirect superclass (ancestor/grandparent) of C
C is the parent of A
Compilation error: chains cannot exceed two classes
questions.explanation: Class A is the indirect superclass (grandparent) of Class C.

questions.question: What property describes how members from Class A flow down through Class B and into Class C?
options: Reflexivity
Transitivity
Polymorphism
Encapsulation
questions.explanation: Inheritance is transitive: accessible members of an ancestor flow down to all descendant subclasses.

questions.question: When 'new C()' is called, in what order are constructors executed?
options: C constructor runs first, then B, then A
A (grandparent) runs first, then B (parent), then C (child)
All constructors execute simultaneously in parallel threads
Only C's constructor executes; ancestor constructors are ignored
questions.explanation: Constructor execution begins at the top of the hierarchy (A) and flows downward to the leaf class (C).

questions.question: Can a leaf class directly access private fields defined in its grandparent class?
options: Yes, multilevel inheritance removes private restrictions
No, private members remain encapsulated and cannot be accessed directly by name
Only if the grandparent class is marked public
Only if the leaf class re-declares them
questions.explanation: Private fields are never directly accessible outside their declaring class, even across multiple inheritance levels.

questions.question: How many objects are created in heap memory when instantiating the leaf class in a 3-tier multilevel chain?
options: Three separate objects
Exactly one object containing state from all three tiers
Zero objects until a method is called
Two objects: one for parent, one for child
questions.explanation: Only one object is created on the heap, containing all inherited and declared fields.

questions.question: If method m() is declared in Grandparent A and overridden in Parent B, which version does Child C execute if C does not override m()?
options: The version in Grandparent A
The version in Parent B
Both versions sequentially
A compilation error occurs
questions.explanation: Java's dispatch looks at the closest ancestor first; Parent B's overridden version is closest to Child C.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of inheritance levels allowed in Java?
options: Exactly 3 levels
Exactly 7 levels
There is no theoretical language limit, though practical design recommends 2 to 4 levels
Maximum 255 levels
questions.explanation: Java imposes no arbitrary limit on inheritance depth, but clean architecture favors shallow hierarchies (2-4 levels).

questions.question: Is multilevel inheritance supported by Java's class system?
options: No, Java only supports single-tier inheritance
Yes, because each class in the chain has only one direct superclass
Only through interfaces
Only in Java 8 and above
questions.explanation: Yes! Because each individual step involves only one direct superclass, Java fully supports multilevel inheritance.

questions.question: What is the ultimate top-level superclass of every multilevel chain in Java?
options: java.lang.System
java.lang.Object
java.lang.Class
java.lang.Chain
questions.explanation: java.lang.Object is at the top of every class hierarchy in Java.

interviewQA.question: What is Multilevel Inheritance and how does it differ from Multiple Inheritance?
interviewQA.answer: Multilevel inheritance is a linear chain where a subclass extends an existing subclass (A -> B -> C). Each class in the chain has exactly one direct superclass, which Java fully supports. Multiple inheritance occurs when a single class directly extends two or more classes simultaneously (C extends A, B), which Java forbids for classes to prevent the Diamond Problem.

interviewQA.question: How does method dispatch resolve when a method is defined in multiple ancestors of a multilevel chain?
interviewQA.answer: Method dispatch follows bottom-up resolution. The runtime JVM checks the actual instance class first. If the method is not found or is not overridden there, it inspects the immediate parent class, and then continues up the ancestor chain. The closest implementation to the leaf class is the one executed.

interviewQA.question: Can a class access a grandparent's overridden method if its immediate parent has already overridden it?
interviewQA.answer: In Java code within the subclass, calling 'super.method()' invokes the immediate parent's version. You cannot write 'super.super.method()' in Java; the language intentionally prohibits skipping levels to maintain encapsulation and the integrity of the immediate parent contract.

interviewQA.question: What are the architectural risks of having deep multilevel inheritance hierarchies?
interviewQA.answer: Deep hierarchies lead to the 'Fragile Base Class' problem, where a small change in a grandparent class can unexpectedly break behavior in leaf classes down the chain. They also increase cognitive load and tight coupling. Modern OOP design favors shallow hierarchies (2-3 levels) and composition where appropriate.

interviewQA.question: Explain transitivity of access modifiers in multilevel inheritance.
interviewQA.answer: Public and protected members remain accessible all the way down the multilevel chain. If Class A declares a protected field, both Class B and Class C can access it. Default (package-private) members are accessible down the chain only as long as all classes remain in the same package. Private members are never accessible directly.

interviewQA.question: How do constructors chain across a multilevel hierarchy?
interviewQA.answer: Constructor invocation chains upward from child to parent to grandparent before executing body statements. When new C() is evaluated, C's constructor calls super() (B's constructor), which calls super() (A's constructor), which calls super() (Object's constructor). The constructor bodies then execute top-down: Object, A, B, and finally C.

activities.title: 10-Point Mastery Checklist: Multilevel Inheritance
checklist: I can define Multilevel Inheritance clearly
I understand the Grandparent -> Parent -> Child relationship structure
I understand transitivity: leaf subclasses inherit all ancestor visible members
I can trace bottom-up method dispatch through 3 or more tiers
I know that only one combined object is created on the heap for the leaf class
I know that constructors execute top-down from Grandparent to Child
I understand why 'super.super' is not permitted in Java
I know how protected fields flow down across all levels
I know the risks of overly deep inheritance hierarchies
I can build a working multilevel hierarchy in Java

practiceProblems.title: Building a 3-Tier Vehicle Hierarchy
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a 3-tier multilevel hierarchy:
1. Grandparent `Vehicle` with `String model` and method `void startEngine()` printing `model + " engine started."`
2. Parent `FourWheeler` extending `Vehicle` with `int wheelCount = 4` and method `void checkTires()` printing `"Inspecting " + wheelCount + " wheels."`
3. Child `Sedan` extending `FourWheeler` with `int trunkCapacityLiters` and method `void openTrunk()` printing `"Opening trunk of " + trunkCapacityLiters + " liters."`
In `Main.main()`, instantiate `Sedan`, set `model = "Camry"` and `trunkCapacityLiters = 450`, then invoke `startEngine()`, `checkTires()`, and `openTrunk()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Camry engine started.
Inspecting 4 wheels.
Opening trunk of 450 liters.
hints: FourWheeler extends Vehicle, and Sedan extends FourWheeler.
Sedan inherits model from Vehicle and checkTires() from FourWheeler.

practiceProblems.title: Academic Person Hierarchy From Scratch
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Write a complete program from scratch demonstrating multilevel inheritance:
1. Grandparent `Person`: field `String name`, method `void introduce()` printing `"My name is " + name`.
2. Parent `Student` extending `Person`: field `String studentId`, method `void study()` printing `name + " (ID: " + studentId + ") is studying."`
3. Child `GraduateStudent` extending `Student`: field `String thesisTopic`, method `void research()` printing `"Researching thesis: " + thesisTopic`.
4. In `Main.main()`, instantiate `GraduateStudent`, set `name = "David"`, `studentId = "G-881"`, `thesisTopic = "Neural Networks"`, and call all three methods.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
My name is David
David (ID: G-881) is studying.
Researching thesis: Neural Networks
hints: GraduateStudent inherits name from Person, and studentId/study() from Student.
Link them with two extends statements.

practiceProblems.title: Multilevel Member Tracking: Electronic Components
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create a multilevel component hierarchy:
1. Grandparent `Electronic`: `protected int voltage = 5`
2. Parent `Microcontroller` extending `Electronic`: `protected int clockSpeedMHz = 16`
3. Child `ArduinoBoard` extending `Microcontroller`:
   - `protected String modelName`
   - Method `public void printSpecs()` printing:
     `"Model: " + modelName + ", Voltage: " + voltage + "V, Clock: " + clockSpeedMHz + " MHz"`
In `Main.main()`, instantiate `ArduinoBoard`, set `modelName = "Uno R3"`, and invoke `printSpecs()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: Model: Uno R3, Voltage: 5V, Clock: 16 MHz
hints: ArduinoBoard has direct access to voltage (from Electronic) and clockSpeedMHz (from Microcontroller) because both are protected.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Broken Multilevel Chain
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The following program has an incorrect inheritance link that breaks the multilevel chain: `Manager` accidentally extends `Person` instead of `Employee`, losing access to `salary` and `work()`. Fix the inheritance declaration so that `Manager` properly extends `Employee` and produces the expected output.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Elena is breathing.
Elena is working for $90000.0
Elena leads a team of 6
hints: Change 'class Manager extends Person' to 'class Manager extends Employee'.
Employee already extends Person, creating the proper 3-tier chain.

practiceProblems.title: Multilevel Game Character Evolution
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a 3-tier role-playing character system:
1. Grandparent `Entity`: `protected String name`, `protected int health`
2. Parent `Hero` extending `Entity`: `protected int mana`, method `public void castSpell(int cost)` reducing `mana` by `cost` and printing `name + " cast spell! Mana left: " + mana`
3. Child `Paladin` extending `Hero`: `protected int armor`, method `public void holyShield()` printing `name + " deployed Holy Shield! Armor: " + armor + ", Health: " + health`
4. Constructors for all 3 classes: `Entity(name, health)`, `Hero(name, health, mana)`, and `Paladin(name, health, mana, armor)` utilizing `super(...)`.
In `Main.main()`, instantiate `Paladin("Arthur", 150, 60, 40)`, invoke `castSpell(20)`, and invoke `holyShield()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Arthur cast spell! Mana left: 40
Arthur deployed Holy Shield! Armor: 40, Health: 150
hints: Each subclass constructor calls super(...) as its very first statement to initialize ancestor fields.
holyShield() accesses fields from all three levels: name and health (Entity), armor (Paladin).
